Team.title: Blue Jays, {from}–{to}
Team.subtitle: Five seasons of the Blue Jays as a team — every number next to the MLB average and the Jays' rank among the 30 clubs that season.
Team.empty: Team numbers haven't been loaded yet.
Team.recordQuestion: Were they as good as their record?
Team.sourcesNote: Runs above or below an average MLB team over the same games: offense = runs scored beyond that average, run prevention = runs not allowed. The two add up to the run differential. About 10 runs is worth one win.
Team.luckNote: Expected record is MLB's own Pythagorean record from runs scored and allowed. Luck = actual wins minus expected wins — usually a strong or weak record in one-run games.
Team.offenseQuestion: How did they score their runs — and how did that compare with the rest of the league?
Team.gridTitle: Where they ranked, season by season
Team.gridNote: Each cell: the Jays' number and their rank among the 30 clubs that season (1st = best), shaded red for strengths and blue for weaknesses. Hover or tap a cell for the MLB average, the league leader and what the stat means.
Team.vsMlbNote: vs MLB: 100 = the MLB average that season (110 = 10% above it). wRC+ is already on that scale; WAR shows the gap to the average club. Shading still follows the rank, so a low K% index is good.

hints.wrc_plus: All-in-one hitting number adjusted for ballpark and league: 100 is average, 120 is 20% better.
hints.ops: On-base percentage plus slugging: getting on base and hitting for power.
hints.obp: How often a hitter reaches base (hits, walks, hit-by-pitch).
hints.slg: Total bases per at-bat — how hard the hits were.
hints.iso: Extra bases per at-bat (SLG minus AVG) — raw power.
hints.babip: Batting average on balls in play — part skill (speed, hard contact), part luck.
hints.k_pct: Share of plate appearances that end in a strikeout. Lower is better.
hints.bb_pct: Share of plate appearances that end in a walk.
hints.whiff_pct: Share of swings that miss the ball. Lower is better.
hints.bat_war: Wins above a replacement-level team from the position players — hitting, running and fielding.
hints.brl_pct: Share of batted balls hit at the ideal speed and angle — the most damaging contact.
hints.hard_hit_pct: Share of batted balls hit 95 mph or harder.
hints.sweet_spot_pct: Share of batted balls launched at 8–32° — line drives and good fly balls.
hints.avg_ev: Average exit velocity (mph) of batted balls.
hints.xwoba: Expected wOBA: what the quality of contact, strikeouts and walks usually produce.
hints.woba: Weighted on-base average: every way of reaching base, weighted by how many runs it is worth.
hints.gb_pct: Ground balls, as a share of balls in play.
hints.ld_pct: Line drives, as a share of balls in play.
hints.fb_pct: Fly balls, as a share of balls in play.
hints.pu_pct: Pop-ups, as a share of balls in play.
hints.ra_per_g: Runs allowed per game. Lower is better.
hints.era: Earned runs allowed per 9 innings. Lower is better.
hints.fip: Fielding-independent pitching: an ERA estimate from strikeouts, walks, hit batters and home runs only. Lower is better.
hints.whip: Walks plus hits allowed per inning. Lower is better.
hints.pit_k_pct: Share of batters faced who struck out.
hints.pit_bb_pct: Share of batters faced who walked. Lower is better.
hints.pit_k_bb_pct: Strikeout rate minus walk rate — one of the best quick reads on pitching quality.
hints.hr9: Home runs allowed per 9 innings. Lower is better.
hints.pit_babip: Batting average allowed on balls in play — pitching, defense and luck mixed together. Lower is better.
hints.pit_whiff_pct: Share of opponents' swings that missed.
hints.pit_war: Wins above a replacement-level staff from the pitchers.
hints.pit_brl_pct: Share of batted balls allowed at the ideal speed and angle. Lower is better.
hints.pit_hard_hit_pct: Share of batted balls allowed at 95 mph or harder. Lower is better.
hints.pit_xwoba: Expected wOBA allowed: what the contact, strikeouts and walks allowed usually produce. Lower is better.
hints.oaa: Outs above average: plays the fielders made beyond what an average defense would, from Statcast.
hints.sp_k_bb_pct: Starters' strikeout rate minus walk rate.
hints.sp_ip_share: Share of the team's innings thrown by starters.
hints.rp_k_bb_pct: Relievers' strikeout rate minus walk rate.

Team.trendsTitle: Five-season trends vs the MLB average
Team.trendsNote: The dashed line is the MLB average that same season — the league moves too (the 2023 rule changes lifted steals and batting averages everywhere), so the gap matters more than the raw number.
Team.contactLuckNote: xwOBA is what the lineup's quality of contact, strikeouts and walks would usually be worth. Results well above it were fortunate (or helped by speed and placement); well below, unlucky. Gaps under .010 are noise.
Team.preventionQuestion: How did they keep runs off the board — the pitching, the contact it allowed, and the defense behind it?
Team.preventionTrendsNote: The dashed line is the MLB average that same season. Lower RA/G, FIP and hard-hit% allowed are better; higher K-BB% is better.
Team.rolesNote: Starters' and relievers' lines, each ranked against the other 29 rotations or bullpens. IP share is the rotation's share of the team's innings — a rotation that goes deep takes work off the bullpen.
Team.eraFipNote: FIP estimates ERA from what pitchers control on their own — strikeouts, walks, hit batters and home runs. A team ERA well above its FIP usually points at the defense or bad sequencing; well below, the reverse. Team OAA (outs above average) is shown for the defense side. Gaps under 0.15 are noise.
Team.eraFipEven: ERA matched FIP: results lined up with the strikeouts, walks and homers.
Team.eraFipWorse: {gap} more runs per 9 innings than FIP predicted — defense or sequencing cost them.
Team.eraFipBetter: {gap} fewer runs per 9 innings than FIP predicted — defense or sequencing helped.
Team.trajectoryQuestion: When did each season turn — and in which situations did they win?
Team.aboveNote: Wins minus losses after every game, lined up by game number: above the line is a winning record. Pick a season (or click its line) to highlight it; the others stay in the background for comparison.
Team.splitsNote: Same splits as each season page. Opponents are sorted by their final winning percentage that season; a blowout is a game decided by 5+ runs.
Team.calloutsQuestion: What defined each season, in MLB ranks?
Team.calloutsTitle: Top-10 and bottom-10 ranks, season by season
Team.calloutsNote: Up to three top-10 and three bottom-10 MLB ranks per season, picked from distinct team skills — scoring, power, plate discipline, speed, quality of contact, run prevention, strikeouts minus walks, home runs allowed, defense, rotation and bullpen — so one strength isn't repeated through closely related stats. Hover a line for what the stat means.
Team.noStrengths: No top-10 ranks in these skills.
Team.noWeaknesses: No bottom-10 ranks in these skills.
Team.glossaryQuestion: How to read the numbers on this page.
Team.methodSeason: Regular season only, the five most recent seasons. Every club's numbers are loaded so each Jays figure can be ranked and set against the league.
Team.methodAverage: The MLB average is the whole league's totals turned into a rate (all runs ÷ all games, and so on) — never an average of 30 team rates.
Team.methodRank: Ranks are among the 30 clubs that season, and 1st is always best — for K%, ERA or runs allowed that means the lowest. Tied clubs share a rank (T-3rd). Colour follows the rank: red for top ranks, blue for bottom ones.
Team.methodRules: Why compare with the league every year: in 2023 MLB added the pitch clock, limited defensive shifts and enlarged the bases. Steals, batting averages and scoring rose everywhere, so a raw 2022-to-2024 change mixes the Jays' own change with the league's.
Team.methodSabermetrics: wRC+ and WAR are FanGraphs figures licensed to MLB: team wRC+ is the plate-appearance-weighted average of the club's hitters, team WAR the sum of its players. FIP is computed from the team's strikeouts, walks, hit batters and home runs with that season's league constant. Expected record is MLB's own Pythagorean record.
Team.methodSources: Sources: MLB Stats API (team and player stats, schedule, standings) and Baseball Savant (Statcast team leaderboards: Barrel%, Hard-hit%, xwOBA, OAA). Updated daily during the season.

WarBreakdown.title: How WAR is built
WarBreakdown.methodology: WAR is built from six run-value components — batting, base running, fielding, positional adjustment, league adjustment, and replacement level — that add up to Runs Above Replacement (RAR). Dividing RAR by the season's runs-per-win (~10) gives WAR. Fielding here is shown separately from the positional adjustment, so a designated hitter's negative positional value is visible on its own bar.

Pitching.title: Pitching Breakdown
Pitching.subtitle: What he throws, where it goes, and how well it works — every regular-season pitch on file.
Pitching.arsenalStory: What he throws and how well it works: Usage is how often he goes to it, Whiff% is how many swings against it miss, and xwOBA (contact) grades how dangerous the contact against it is — lower means weaker contact.
Pitching.xwobaConNote: xwOBA here covers batted balls only — strikeouts and walks are not part of contact quality.
Pitching.movementStory: How far each pitch breaks compared to a pitch with no spin (the dashed crosshair). The bold ringed dots mark each pitch type's average break.
Pitching.pitcherViewNote: Shown from the pitcher's point of view; units are inches of break.
Pitching.veloTrendStory: Average velocity of his main fastball in each game this season — a slow multi-week slide of 1–2 mph is often the first sign of fatigue.
Pitching.locationStory: Where his pitches cross the zone — darker means more pitches to that spot.
Pitching.zoneEraNote: Savant moved its plate-coordinate origin in 2026, so the location heatmap shows one era at a time.
Pitching.rvNote: RV/100 = Savant run value per 100 pitches for the whole season, every club (positive = runs saved = good). Shown only for a full single season without month or batter filters.

Fielding.explainTitle: How to read FRV and OAA
Fielding.explainBody: FRV (Fielding Run Value) is how many runs the player saved or cost their team with their glove compared to a league-average fielder at the same position. +5 is excellent, 0 is average, −5 is poor. OAA (Outs Above Average) is the underlying count of plays made above the league rate.
Fielding.note: Source: Baseball Savant via pybaseball. Catcher framing and pitcher PFP use different metrics and are not shown here.
